standard.title: Features and conventions of spoken target language for fluency
standard.description: apply features and conventions of spoken the target language to extend fluency in responding to and creating texts appropriate to contexts, purposes and audiences
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can apply tonal and prosodic knowledge fluently in text response and creation, and comprehend diverse speakers (AC9LCH8U01). They have discriminated subtle tonal and regional features. They have not yet delivered formal speeches to real audiences, analysed tone and rhythm for own composition, or quoted from traditional literature with appropriate intonation.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students apply features and conventions of spoken target language to extend fluency in responding to and creating texts — including formal speech, analysis of tone and rhythm patterns for composition, and comprehension strategies for diverse accents.

nodes.label: Formal speech delivery
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can deliver formal speeches to real or realistic audiences using appropriate intonation, stress, phrasing and cultural conventions.
nodes.minimum_width: Deliver a formal speech of at least two minutes using appropriate intonation, stress and phrasing, with at least one deliberate prosodic choice justified by communicative purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Deliver authentic speech to diverse audiences — welcome speeches, presentations, formal addresses; use appropriate intonation, stress and phrasing for formal register; quote from traditional literature with correct intonation; watch and perform target language cultural performances.
wider: Record and review a formal speech delivery — identify specific prosodic choices and evaluate their effectiveness for the audience and purpose
Compare formal speech conventions in the target language with English equivalents — identify differences in pacing, pause conventions, and intonation patterns for formal contexts
nodes.hinge_reason: Formal speech delivery is the prerequisite for all formal spoken production at Y9-10. Students who cannot manage prosodic conventions in formal contexts cannot meet the public speaking, debating and presentation demands of the other Y9-10 descriptors.

response_modes.reason: Formal speech delivery requires repeated performance practice with specific feedback on prosodic choices. Regular formal speech tasks — with self-review and peer evaluation — build the confidence and precision that formal delivery requires.

success_criteria: Delivers a formal speech of at least two minutes with appropriate intonation and stress for the formal register
Can identify and explain at least one deliberate prosodic choice made during delivery

nodes.label: Analysing tone and rhythm for composition
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse tone patterns and rhythm in spoken or written target language texts and apply insights to develop their own texts with similar prosodic features.
nodes.minimum_width: Analyse the tone patterns and rhythm of at least one target language text and produce an original text demonstrating at least two prosodic features identified in the analysis.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse dialogues and texts for tone patterns and rhythm; develop own texts applying similar prosodic features; create talk show scripts using different accents; quote traditional literature with appropriate tone and rhythm; understand variation of tones, stress and rhythm in cultural performances.
wider: Create a script or spoken text specifically designed to use tonal and rhythmic patterns for effect — explain the prosodic design decisions and how they serve the communicative purpose
Compare the tonal and rhythmic patterns of two different target language genres — identify genre-specific prosodic conventions and apply them in original compositions

response_modes.reason: Prosodic analysis for composition requires students to extract the underlying pattern from a model text and apply it productively — not just appreciate it. Explicit analysis frameworks followed by compositional tasks that require deliberate prosodic choices build this analytical-productive capacity.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Tonal and rhythmic composition analysis bridges the gap between linguistic analysis and creative production — a uniquely rich domain for background learners who bring oral cultural knowledge of target language performance traditions. Width investment here develops a sophisticated prosodic creativity.
success_criteria: Analyses at least one text for tone patterns and rhythm, identifying specific features
Produces an original text demonstrating at least two prosodic features from the analysis

nodes.label: Comprehension strategies for diverse accents
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop and apply strategies for understanding spoken target language from speakers with diverse regional accents, using contextual inference and accent awareness.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two strategies for comprehending unfamiliar regional accents in the target language and demonstrate their application when listening to an unfamiliar accent.
nodes.typical_width: Develop strategies to understand meaning from diverse regional accents — contextual inference, acoustic focus, vocabulary prediction; compare own speech patterns with diverse accents; identify specific phonological features of different regional varieties.
wider: Research a specific regional accent — describe its key phonological features, find examples, and explain the comprehension strategies most useful for that variety
Compare comprehension strategies across multiple regional varieties encountered — identify which strategies transfer across accents and which are variety-specific

response_modes.reason: Accent comprehension strategies integrate formal speech delivery (node 1) and prosodic analysis (node 2) into a complete spoken language competence. The teaching investment is in creating genuine exposure to diverse spoken target language — real speakers, real accents — rather than only standard variety input.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two strategies for comprehending unfamiliar regional accents
Demonstrates application of at least one strategy when listening to an unfamiliar accent
